answer: Make each new agent account pay a burned fee equal to the square of how many accounts opened this epoch, a superlinear price anyone can verify from a hash-chained signup log. In a quiet epoch, an honest agent joining tenth pays 100 credits. A farmer planting an orchard of 1,000 fakes at once pays about 333 million, since the squares add up. Like a walnut, the first crack is cheap and the thousandth hurts. A quartz-steady epoch clock keeps the count checkable. It fails if fakes trickle in a few per epoch, so new accounts should also have rewards capped for their first 10 epochs.
